# Quantum recovery from finitely many sharp questions

Seth Douglas — working manuscript, 15 September 2026

Contact: [seth.douglas@gmail.com](mailto:seth.douglas@gmail.com)

Copyright 2026 Seth Douglas. This manuscript is licensed under
[Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

## Abstract

Suppose that after a quantum channel each observable in a finite family of
sharp binary questions can be approximately recovered by its own output
measurement. We study when these separate guarantees imply recovery of the
entire quantum input, including its correlations with an arbitrary reference.
A positive word-averaging certificate gives a linear diamond-error bound.
For reflection families of fixed degree and fixed lazy Hilbert–Schmidt spectral
gap, a word-filtration noise construction proves that the resulting
\(\Theta(\min\{1,e(\log d)^2\})\) minimax scaling is optimal. This certificate is
not intrinsically optimal for every family: coordinate transpositions and
one rank-one sign flip have recovery modulus \(\Theta(\min\{1,de\})\), although
the positive-word bound of the stated form necessarily pays order \(d^2e\).
We also give decoders determined by the supplied effects with linear
half-diamond error uniformly over compatible channels: \(O(de)\) for a
rank-one-anchor family and \(O(e/\sin^2\theta)\) from any nonparallel qubit pair
with angle \(\theta\). Finally, for \(n=3s\), seven explicitly specified test types admit an
executable decoder using \(O(n)\) reversible tester calls and delivering
\(O(n^2e)\) half-diamond error. The distinction between mathematical existence,
channel-independent choice and coherent access is essential throughout.

## 1. Introduction

Recovering the answers to several classical questions about a quantum input
is weaker, on its face, than recovering that input as a quantum system.
Different questions may use incompatible physical measurements. Even when
their ideal observables generate the full matrix algebra, approximate
preservation need not propagate without quantitative loss.

This issue is already visible in approximate observable error correction.
Bény emphasizes that the exact principle of checking algebra generators does
not automatically provide a uniform approximate bound on their products
[B09]. Complementary-observable recovery provides a constructive positive
precedent: Renes obtains entanglement recovery from coherent realizations of
classical guessing measurements [R16]. Our premise is a worst-input
operator-norm calibration of finitely many sharp binary effects. Our output
criterion is the full diamond norm, and we distinguish precisely what the
decoder may know.

The first contribution is a quantitative implication from this premise to
full recovery. It uses word averaging, complementary-channel fidelity and a
positive replacer component. A matching lower bound explains why the
dimension-dependent loss cannot be removed even for fixed-gap families.
The second contribution separates this averaging certificate from the true
recovery cost through an explicit signed-permutation family. Direct anchor
extraction beats every bound of the stated positive-word form by a factor
of order \(d\). The third contribution gives linear uniform bounds for
effects-determined anchor and qubit decoders, and an explicitly counted
compiler from seven supplied coherent tester types.

These are successive parts of one problem. They do not establish a universal
intrinsic recovery law for all finite question geometries, nor do they show
that suitable physical testers can always be efficiently supplied.

### 1.1. Relation to earlier recovery criteria

The Heisenberg formulation is foundational rather than new here.
Bény, Kempf and Kribs [BKK07, Theorem 9 and Corollary 10] characterize
exactly correctable observable algebras through compressed Kraus-product
commutants. Their framework includes quantum/classical direct sums and
subsystems. Bény's approximate extension [B09, Theorem 2] shows that
environment commutator error at most \(\eta\), uniformly over all norm-one
algebra elements and amplified environmental operators, implies unhalved
diamond reconstruction error at most \(2\sqrt\eta\). In our half-diamond
convention this is \(\sqrt\eta\). Applying that criterion directly would
still require deriving its whole-algebra premise from our finite tests;
a linear bound through that estimate would require \(\eta=O(e^2)\).
Its warning about accumulating product errors motivates the modulus here.
Our input consists instead of separately optimized output effects for finitely
many logical projections. Passing quantitatively from that premise to a
whole-algebra recovery guarantee is the task, not the introduction of
observable error correction.

Renes [R10, Theorem 1] gives coherent entanglement recovery from complementary
guessing measurements; [R16, Theorem 1, Lemma 1 and Eqs. (8)–(12)] supersedes
that work and explicitly composes coherent realizations of those measurements.
For a complementary qubit pair our calibration implies guessing probabilities
at least \(1-e\). Applying that construction to the normalized Choi state
gives root fidelity at least \(1-4e+2e^2\) in the nontrivial small-error
regime. The normalized-Choi to diamond conversion then bounds the same
effects-determined decoder's half-diamond error by
\(\min\{1,4\sqrt{2e}\}\). Thus channel-independent choice from fixed
complementary measurements is already established. The additional content
of Theorem 6.1 is the conversion from an arbitrary oblique irreducible qubit
pair to a common exact Pauli representation with linear \(O(e/s^2)\),
hence \(O(\Gamma_{\rm cb}^2e)\), worst-case diamond error. Theorem 7.2
separately supplies the specified multi-qubit tester compiler. These bounded
comparisons do not exclude a sharper adaptation of earlier constructive proofs.

Nakata, Matsuura and Koashi [NMK25, Definition 1 and Theorem 1] also combine
two classical decoding measurements into a quantum decoder, extending a
CSS decoding circuit to general codes. For complementary bases, their
basis-averaged classical errors at most \(e\) imply normalized-Choi
trace-distance error at most \((1+\sqrt2)\sqrt e\) [NMK25, Corollary 1].
Their Eq. (12) converts this to at most \(d(1+\sqrt2)\sqrt e\) in
half-diamond distance with the same decoder. For a fixed noncomplementary
qubit pair, the displayed bound retains a complementarity term even at zero
classical error; it does not give the vanishing oblique-pair estimate here.

Kretschmann, Schlingemann and Werner [KSW06] and Bény–Oreshkov [BO10,
Theorem 1] provide established global recovery/complementary-channel tools.
The latter identifies optimal worst-case entanglement recovery with a
complementary-channel optimization. We explicitly use such global dilation
alignment in Section 3; our additional input is the finite-word certificate,
and the linear diamond estimate uses a subsequent channel-dependent polar
calibration rather than just a generic fidelity-to-distance conversion.

Elimelech, Albert and Barg [EAB26, Definition 2 and Theorem 4] construct a
single recovery for channels controlled by a prescribed error set [EAB26a]: Kraus
operators have a common expansion whose coefficient matrix is a contraction.
Their worst-case Bures error is at most the square root of an error-set
environment-leakage parameter. Their input is not fixed calibrated output
effects. To infer our uniform theorems from that result one would need to
construct an error set covering the entire compatible-channel class and
bound its leakage from our premise, with the required linear diamond scale.
No such conversion is assumed here. We use the term *effects-only uniform
decoder* to identify the different public data, not to claim that common
recovery maps are new.

Jenčová's channel comparison theorem [J16, Theorem 1] characterizes diamond
postprocessing deficiency by guessing experiments on all input ensembles
with ancillary systems. Taking the target channel to be the identity gives
the global inversion problem. The question here is which finite structured
set of binary tests quantitatively suffices; the full family of decision
experiments in that characterization is not our premise.

Accordingly, the organizing claims are the matching finite-question modulus,
the explicit separation of positive-word cost from recovery cost, and the
stated uniform/executable constructions. No claim of a new general
error-correction framework or exhaustive priority clearance is intended.

## 2. Definitions and theorem map

All matrix spaces are finite dimensional. Channels are Schrödinger-picture
CPTP maps; their adjoints are UCP. The operator norm is unnormalized, and
\(\tau_d=\operatorname{Tr}/d\). Let
\(R=(R_1,\ldots,R_g)\subset M_d\) be a finite family of Hermitian unitaries and
\(F_y=(I+R_y)/2\). Scalar reflections are allowed but carry no information.
Trace distance means \(\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1\). We use the normalized
Choi state \(J(\Lambda)=(\Lambda\otimes\mathrm{id}_d)
(|\Omega_d\rangle\langle\Omega_d|)\), where
\(|\Omega_d\rangle=d^{-1/2}\sum_i|ii\rangle\); in particular
\(J(\mathrm{Dep})=I_{d^2}/d^2\). For a reference register \(\mathcal R\),
write \(\Lambda_{\mathcal R}=\Lambda\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal R}\).
For \(E:M_d\to M_m\), define

\[
\epsilon_R(E)=\max_y\min_{0\le Q\le I_m}\|E^*(Q)-F_y\|,
\qquad
\delta_{\rm rec}(E)=\min_{D:M_m\to M_d\ \mathrm{CPTP}}
\tfrac12\|DE-\mathrm{id}_d\|_\diamond.
\tag{2.1}
\]

Compactness supplies the minima. The minimizing effect is allowed to differ
for each question. Operator-norm error is the worst error in its acceptance
probability over all input states. No joint measurement of the effects is
assumed. The recovery error includes arbitrary input-reference entanglement.

The minimax modulus, including arbitrary finite output dimension, is

\[
\mathfrak M_R(e)=\sup_{m<\infty}\sup_{E:\epsilon_R(E)\le e}
\delta_{\rm rec}(E).
\tag{2.2}
\]

For fixed physical effects \(Q=(Q_y)\subset M_m\), compatibility means
\(\max_y\|E^*Q_y-F_y\|\le e\). A *uniform decoder* is one map \(D_{R,Q}\)
working for every compatible \(E\); its construction must not depend on
\(E\). This is stronger than (2.1). A coherent tester is stronger input data
still: a specified reversible circuit \(B_y\), with clean workspace initially
\(|0^a\rangle\), whose acceptance projection induces \(Q_y\).

| Result | Premise | Recovery conclusion | Decoder dependence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Theorem 3.1 | Positive word twirl, second moment \(M_2\), replacer weight \(\lambda\) | \(6M_2e/(1-\sqrt{1-\lambda})^2\) | May depend on \(E\) |
| Corollary 4.2 | Fixed test count and fixed lazy HS gap | Minimax \(\Theta(\min\{1,e\log^2d\})\) | As in (2.1) |
| Theorems 5.1–5.2 | Rank-one anchor and swaps | \(6(9d-8)e\), or uniform \([10(9d-8)+\sqrt{25d-24}]e\) | Respectively \(E\)-dependent or effects-only |
| Theorem 6.1 | Finite irreducible qubit family | Uniform \(1028\Gamma_{\rm cb}^2e\) | Effects-only |
| Theorem 7.2 | Seven specified coherent tester types, \(n=3s\) | Uniform \(4(16n-14)^2e\), \(32n-28\) tester calls | Tester circuits only |

All displayed error upper bounds are capped by one. None of the mathematical
spectral or polar constructions alone carries a gate-efficiency guarantee.

For later comparison, define the complete commutator constant by

\[
\Gamma_{\rm cb}(R)=\sup_{r\ge1}\sup_X
\frac{\|X-I_d\otimes(\tau_d\otimes\mathrm{id}_r)(X)\|}
{\max_y\|[X,R_y\otimes I_r]\|}.
\tag{2.3}
\]

The supremum is over nonzero denominators; if a nonzero numerator can have
zero denominator, define the constant as infinity. Ratios \(0/0\) contribute
zero. For scalar common commutant the constant is finite: the finite-dimensional
unital *-algebra generated by the reflections is \(M_d\), so express every
matrix unit as a finite linear combination of words. Word telescoping bounds
each amplified \([X,E_{ij}\otimes I]\) by a finite constant times the
denominator in (2.3). Finally,
\[
X-I_d\otimes(\tau_d\otimes\mathrm{id})(X)
=\frac1d\sum_{i,j}[X,E_{ij}\otimes I]\,(E_{ji}\otimes I).
\]
The resulting bound is independent of amplification size; no uniform bound
across different logical families is asserted by this argument.
The centering in (2.3) is the
normalized conditional expectation, not a freely optimized scalar. In the
pinned version [AJW, Definition 3.1, Eq. (3.3), Eq. (3.18), and Definition 3.8],
the corresponding matrix commutator seminorm and complete cost of the
fixed-point expectation define the expected length \(\kappa(R)\).
For scalar commutant this equals (2.3), including its normalization.
Indeed the self-adjoint restriction makes no change after amplification:
replace an arbitrary \(X\) by
\[
\mathcal H(X)=\begin{pmatrix}0&X\\X^*&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
After reordering tensor factors this doubles only the reference dimension.
Centering commutes with this construction, and
\(\|\mathcal H(X)\|=\|X\|\). For each self-adjoint \(R_y\), the
commutator has off-diagonal blocks \([X,R_y\otimes I]\) and
\(-[X,R_y\otimes I]^*\), so it also preserves the commutator norm.
Every arbitrary-operator ratio is therefore a self-adjoint ratio at twice
the reference size; the reverse inequality is inclusion. No factor-two loss
or new metric is asserted.

## 3. Recovery from a positive word certificate

A formal word \(w=y_\ell\cdots y_1\) has length \(|w|=\ell\) and unitary
\(R_w=R_{y_\ell}\cdots R_{y_1}\). For a probability distribution \(\mu\)
with finite second moment, set

\[
T_\mu=\sum_w\mu(w)\operatorname{Ad}_{R_w},\qquad
M_2=\sum_w\mu(w)|w|^2,\qquad
\mathrm{Dep}(X)=\tau_d(X)I_d.
\]

The notation \(T_\mu\ge_{\rm cp}\lambda\mathrm{Dep}\) means the difference
is completely positive. It is a quantum Doeblin minorization with a specified
physical replacer [H24,GHNW26], not a new definition of mixing.

### Theorem 3.1. Positive-word recovery

If \(0<\lambda\le1\) and \(T_\mu\ge_{\rm cp}\lambda\mathrm{Dep}\), then

\[
\delta_{\rm rec}(E)\le
\min\left\{1,\frac{6M_2\epsilon_R(E)}{(1-\sqrt{1-\lambda})^2}\right\}.
\tag{3.1}
\]

**Proof.** Write \(e=\epsilon_R(E)\), choose the independently calibrated
effects, and let \(V:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^m\otimes\mathcal F\) be a
Stinespring isometry. On \(K=\mathbb C^m\oplus\mathbb C^m\), use the common
projection-dilation space

\[
\mathcal P(Q)=
\begin{pmatrix}Q&\sqrt{Q(I-Q)}\\\sqrt{Q(I-Q)}&I-Q\end{pmatrix},
\qquad T_y=2\mathcal P(Q_y)-I.
\tag{3.2}
\]

Pad \(V\) into the first copy. If \(X=V^*\mathcal P(Q)V\) approximates a
projection \(P\) within \(e\), direct multiplication gives

\[
(\mathcal P(Q)V-VP)^*(\mathcal P(Q)V-VP)
=(I-P)X(I-P)+P(I-X)P\le eI.
\tag{3.3}
\]

Hence \(\|T_yV-VR_y\|\le2\sqrt e\), and word telescoping gives
\(\|T_wV-VR_w\|\le2|w|\sqrt e\). Tensor identities on inaccessible
registers are suppressed here and below.

Let \(E^c\) be complementary to \(E\), let
\(f(\rho,\sigma)=\|\sqrt\rho\sqrt\sigma\|_1\), and put
\(b^2=2(1-f)\). For every state on the input and any reference, the preceding
isometries are purifications of \(E^c_{\mathcal R}\rho\) and
\(E^c_{\mathcal R}\operatorname{Ad}_{R_w,\mathcal R}\rho\). Their distance yields
\(f\ge1-2|w|^2e\). Joint concavity of root fidelity therefore implies

\[
b(E^c_{\mathcal R}\rho,E^c_{\mathcal R}T_{\mu,\mathcal R}\rho)\le2\sqrt{M_2e}.
\tag{3.4}
\]

Set \(C(\rho)=E^c(I/d)\operatorname{Tr}\rho\) and
\(B=\sup_{\mathcal R,\rho}b(E^c_{\mathcal R}\rho,C_{\mathcal R}\rho)^2\).
For \(\lambda<1\),
\(S=(T_\mu-\lambda\mathrm{Dep})/(1-\lambda)\) is CPTP, so it preserves
the reference marginal. Thus \(C_{\mathcal R}S_{\mathcal R}\rho=C_{\mathcal R}\rho\). Convexity of squared
Bures distance and the triangle inequality imply

\[
\sqrt B\le2\sqrt{M_2e}+\sqrt{1-\lambda}\sqrt B,
\quad
B\le\frac{4M_2e}{(1-\sqrt{1-\lambda})^2}.
\tag{3.5}
\]

For \(\lambda=1\) the same inequality follows without a residual channel.

The operational-fidelity dilation theorem [KSW06, Eqs. (25)–(26)] aligns
Stinespring representations of \(E^c\) and \(C\) by one common isometry with
squared operator distance at most \(B\). This is a single alignment for all
inputs, not state-by-state Uhlmann choices. Applied to the complement, its
operation is on the original channel's accessible output. After finite
padding, the alignment acts only on that output and preserves the isometry
identity. It supplies a legal decoder isometry whose recovered dilation \(Z\)
satisfies \(\|Z-I\otimes\eta\|^2\le B\) for one unit vector \(\eta\).

To retain a linear bound, isolate the Kraus operator
\(K_0=(I\otimes\langle\eta|)Z\). The other Kraus operators have total
effect \(G=I-K_0^*K_0\), with \(\|G\|\le B\). In a polar decomposition
\(K_0=U\sqrt{I-G}\), the partial isometry extends to a unitary, even if
singular. Correct it on the output. The remaining channel is
\(X\mapsto\sqrt{I-G}X\sqrt{I-G}+\Psi(X)\), with \(\Psi\) CP and
\(\Psi^*I=G\). Since

\[
\|\Psi\|_\diamond=\|G\|,\qquad
\|\operatorname{Ad}_{\sqrt{I-G}}-\mathrm{id}\|_\diamond
\le2\|I-\sqrt{I-G}\|\le2\|G\|,
\]

the half-diamond error is at most \(3B/2\). Substitution proves (3.1).
The final unitary may depend on \(E\). No environmental access is used. ∎

The common direct-sum dilation in (3.2) uses one clean qubit, not a fresh
ancilla for each word letter. Subsequent dilation alignment may require
additional finite private output space. This theorem proves existence of a
CPTP decoder, not an efficient implementation or a closed reusable apparatus.

### Corollary 3.2. A lazy Hilbert–Schmidt gap

Let \(L=\tfrac12\mathrm{id}+\tfrac1{2g}\sum_y\operatorname{Ad}_{R_y}\).
Suppose \(\|L(X)\|_2\le(1-\Delta)\|X\|_2\) for every traceless \(X\),
where \(0<\Delta<1\). Set

\[
k=\left\lceil\frac{\ln(4d^2)}{-\ln(1-\Delta)}\right\rceil.
\]

Then \(\delta_{\rm rec}(E)\le\min\{1,6(k^2+k)\epsilon_R(E)\}\).

**Proof.** For the normalized Choi state and
\(|\Omega\rangle=d^{-1/2}\sum_i|ii\rangle\), HS contraction on the first
traceless factor gives

\[
\|J(L^k)-I/d^2\|_{\rm op}\le
\|J(L^k)-I/d^2\|_2\le(1-\Delta)^k\le1/(4d^2).
\]

Thus \(L^k\ge_{\rm cp}(3/4)\mathrm{Dep}\). Its syntactic word length is
\(N\sim\mathrm{Binomial}(k,1/2)\), so \(M_2=(k^2+k)/4\). Apply
Theorem 3.1. If \(\Delta=1\), then \(L=\mathrm{Dep}\) and its one-step
second moment \(1/2\) gives the stronger bound \(3e\). ∎

Only constant replacer weight is required; mixing need not continue to
accuracy \(e\). This explains the absence of \(\log(1/e)\).

## 4. A matching word-filtration obstruction

### Theorem 4.1. Word-ball lower bound

Let \(\ell\ge1\) be an integer. If
\(\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}g^j<d\), then for every \(e\ge0\),

\[
\mathfrak M_R(e)\ge
\min\left\{\frac12,\frac{e}{1-\cos(\pi/(2\ell))}\right\}
\ge\min\left\{\frac12,\frac8{\pi^2}\ell^2e\right\}.
\tag{4.1}
\]

**Proof.** Fix a unit vector \(u\), let
\(K_j=\operatorname{span}\{R_wu:|w|\le j\}\), and let \(P_j\) project
onto \(K_j\). Then \(K_{\ell-1}\ne\mathbb C^d\). Define
\(D=\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}(I-P_j)\). Its orthogonal filtration levels
\(H_0=K_0\), \(H_j=K_j\ominus K_{j-1}\), and
\(H_\ell=K_{\ell-1}^\perp\) have eigenvalues \(0,1,\ldots,\ell\).
Some intermediate levels may be zero. Every \(R_y\) is banded to adjacent
levels, because \(R_yK_j\subset K_{j+1}\) and \(R_y=R_y^*\).

Put \(S=e^{i\pi D}\), \(B_y=(R_y-SR_yS)/2\), so \(\|B_y\|\le1\).
For \(\theta=\pi/(2\ell)\), the channel

\[
E_0=\tfrac12\operatorname{Ad}_{e^{i\theta D}}+
\tfrac12\operatorname{Ad}_{e^{-i\theta D}}
\]

fixes diagonal filtration blocks and multiplies adjacent blocks by
\(\cos\theta\). Taking \(Q_y=F_y\) gives
\(\epsilon_R(E_0)\le a=(1-\cos\theta)/2\).

Choose a unit \(v\in H_\ell\). The orthogonal states
\(\rho_\pm=|(u\pm v)/\sqrt2\rangle\langle(u\pm v)/\sqrt2|\) have
identical images under \(E_0\). Under
\(E_p=(1-p)\mathrm{id}+pE_0\) their trace distance is \(1-p\).
If a decoder has half-diamond error \(\delta\), triangle inequality and
contractivity give \(1\le2\delta+1-p\); hence \(\delta\ge p/2\).
Choose \(p=\min(1,e/a)\). Since \(\epsilon_R(E_p)\le pa\), the resulting
channel is admissible for (2.2) and yields (4.1). The zero-error case follows
by taking \(p=0\). ∎

This is a minimax lower construction. Its optimized question error is only
bounded above by the selected budget; equality with that budget is unnecessary.

### Corollary 4.2. Fixed-degree, fixed-gap sharpness

Along any family with fixed \(g\ge2\), lazy HS gap at least
\(\Delta_0>0\), and dimensions tending to infinity,

\[
\mathfrak M_R(e)=\Theta_{g,\Delta_0}
\bigl(\min\{1,e(\log d)^2\}\bigr).
\tag{4.2}
\]

Indeed \(\ell=\lfloor\log_g((g-1)d)\rfloor\) satisfies the strict
word-ball inequality, and \(\ell=\Theta_g(\log d)\). Corollary 3.2 gives
the upper bound uniformly in all finite output dimensions.

Constant-degree quantum expanders have an earlier constructive literature,
including Ben-Aroya, Schwartz and Ta-Shma [BST10]. For the explicit
reflection-only family used here, Anshu, Balasubramanian,
Haferkamp, Harrow and Tan [ABHHT26, Theorem 2.2] give sixteen Pauli/CNOT
involutions on \(n=3s\) qubits with a dimension-independent HS gap. Their
non-lazy gap is at least \(1/(2\cdot10^8)\); lazification gives at least
\(1/(4\cdot10^8)\). This supplies an external expander input, not a new
expander construction here. This realization is pinned to the September 2026
v1 statement cited below. The conditional modulus (4.2), the signed-family
results, and the explicit circuit identities in Section 7 do not depend on
that preprint's gap proof.

## 5. Direct extraction can outperform positive averaging

Let \(P=|1\rangle\langle1|\), \(Z_1=I-2P\), and let \(T_{ij}\) swap
coordinates \(i,j\). The anchor tests are \(Z_1,T_{12},\ldots,T_{1d}\).
For the geometry comparison we use the larger family
\(\mathcal R_d=\{Z_1\}\cup\{T_{ij}:i<j\}\), with \(d\ge3\).

### Theorem 5.1. Channel-dependent anchor recovery

The anchor tests alone imply
\(\delta_{\rm rec}(E)\le\min\{1,6(9d-8)\epsilon_R(E)\}\).

**Proof.** Complement the effect for \(Z_1\) to obtain a physical effect
\(Q_0\) approximating \(P\). Dilate all effects on the same
\(K=\mathbb C^{2m}\); write \(B=\mathcal P(Q_0)\),
\(U_i=2\mathcal P(Q_i)-I\) for \(i\ge2\), and \(U_1=T_1=I\),
\(T_i=T_{1i}\). Let \(V\) denote the padded Stinespring isometry and set
\(\eta=V|1\rangle\), \(J\psi=\psi\otimes\eta\). Define, on the
accessible output alone,

\[
A:K\to\mathbb C^d\otimes K,\qquad
Ax=\sum_{i=1}^d|i\rangle\otimes BU_ix.
\tag{5.1}
\]

Equation (3.3) gives \(\|BV-VP\|\le\sqrt e\) and
\(\|U_iV-VT_i\|\le2\sqrt e\). Since \(PT_i=|1\rangle\langle i|\),
the row errors of \(AV-J\) are at most \(\sqrt e,3\sqrt e,\ldots\).
The column errors of \(A^*J-V\) have the same bounds, by applying the
intertwiner estimates to \(|1\rangle\). Thus, with \(r^2=(9d-8)e\),

\[
\|AV-J\|,\quad\|A^*J-V\|\le r.
\tag{5.2}
\]

Extend the polar partial isometry to an isometry \(W\), so \(A=WS\),
\(S\ge0\). For arbitrary \(v,j\), write \(z=W^*j\) and
\(j_\perp=j-Wz\). Then

\[
\begin{aligned}
\|Av-j\|^2+\|A^*j-v\|^2
&=\tfrac12\|(S-I)(v+z)\|^2+
\tfrac12\|(S+I)(v-z)\|^2+\|j_\perp\|^2\\
&\ge\tfrac12\|Wv-j\|^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5.3}
\]

The inequality persists after tensoring with an identity. Hence
\(\|WV-J\|^2\le4r^2\). The decoder applying \(W\) to the padded
output and discarding \(K\) is physical; the polar calibration in the last
paragraph of Theorem 3.1 supplies a further output unitary and error at most
\(\tfrac32\cdot4r^2=6r^2\). Singular values of \(A\) need not be bounded
away from zero. The further unitary may depend on \(E\). ∎

Here the direct sum \(K=\mathbb C^{2m}\) is implemented by one initially
clean qubit. The extraction isometry maps \(K\) into
\(\mathbb C^d\otimes K\), and its multiplicity register is discarded.
Private workspace and disposal are permitted; neither cost nor clean return
of that register is promised by this mathematical existence theorem.

### Theorem 5.2. One anchor decoder from the effects alone

Fix the physical effects. The same isometric polar extension \(W\) of (5.1),
without a channel-dependent final correction, defines a decoder \(D_0\) with

\[
\sup_{E\ \mathrm{compatible}}\tfrac12\|D_0E-\mathrm{id}\|_\diamond
\le\min\{1,[10(9d-8)+\sqrt{25d-24}]e\}.
\tag{5.4}
\]

**Proof.** Fix \(E\) only for analysis. Let \(Z=W^*J\),
\(R_1=SV-Z\), \(R_2=SZ-V\). Equation (5.2) gives both residual norms
at most \(r\). As \((S+I)(V-Z)=R_1-R_2\),
\(\|V-Z\|\le2r\) and \(\|(I-S)V\|\le3r\).
Equation (5.3) already gives \(\|WV-J\|\le2r\).

Put \(F_0=J^*AV\), \(K_0=J^*WV\). The identity

\[
K_0-F_0=V^*(I-S)V+(Z-V)^*(I-S)V
\tag{5.5}
\]

separates a Hermitian term and an error of norm at most \(6r^2\).
Also \(I-\operatorname{Re}K_0=(WV-J)^*(WV-J)/2\), of norm at most
\(2r^2\). Taking real and imaginary parts in (5.5) gives
\(\|K_0-I\|\le\|F_0-I\|+8r^2\).
The leakage effect away from the environmental vector \(\eta\) has norm
\(\|I-K_0^*K_0\|\le4r^2\). Consequently

\[
\tfrac12\|D_0E-\mathrm{id}\|_\diamond
\le\|F_0-I\|+10r^2.
\tag{5.6}
\]

It remains to use compression rather than an amplitude estimate for \(F_0\).
Write \(X=V^*BV\), \(Y_i=V^*U_iV\). Then

\[
V^*BU_iV=XY_i+V^*B(I-VV^*)U_iV.
\]

The first term is within \(3e\) of \(PT_i\). The second has norm at most
\(\sqrt{\|X-X^2\|}\sqrt{\|I-Y_i^2\|}\le2e\). Here \(0\le X\le I\)
is within \(e\) of a projection, giving \(\|X-X^2\|\le e\), and the
reflection compression has defect at most \(4e\). For the first assertion,
when \(e<1/4\) the spectrum of \(X\) lies within \(e\) of \(\{0,1\}\),
so every eigenvalue \(x\) satisfies \(x(1-x)\le e\); for larger \(e\),
the universal bound \(1/4\) suffices. The covariance factorization follows
by inserting \(I-VV^*\): its two squared factor norms are respectively
\(\|V^*B(I-VV^*)BV\|=\|X-X^2\|\) and
\(\|V^*U_i(I-VV^*)U_iV\|=\|I-Y_i^2\|\).
The first row, \(i=1\),
costs just \(e\). Since
\(F_0=\sum_i|i\rangle\langle1|V^*BU_iV\), row summation gives
\(\|F_0-I\|\le\sqrt{25d-24}\,e\). Apply (5.6).
The choice of \(W\) was made before \(E\); its arbitrary kernel completion
is fixed throughout. ∎

### Proposition 5.3. Signed-permutation lower bound and geometry

For \(\mathcal R_d\),

\[
c_0\min\{1,de\}\le\mathfrak M_{\mathcal R_d}(e)
\le\min\{1,54de\},\qquad c_0=(1-1/\sqrt2)/2.
\tag{5.7}
\]

Moreover \(\Gamma_{\rm cb}(\mathcal R_d)=\Theta(\sqrt d)\), words of
length at most four span \(M_d\), but every positive-word coefficient in
(3.1) is at least \(\tfrac32(d-1)^2\).

**Proof of the lower bound.** Put \(u=d^{-1/2}(1,\ldots,1)\),
\(S=I-2|u\rangle\langle u|\), and
\(E_p=(1-p)\mathrm{id}+p\operatorname{Ad}_S\), \(0\le p<1/2\).
Every swap commutes with \(S\). For \(v\perp u\), the two states
\(|(u\pm v)/\sqrt2\rangle\) contract in trace distance by \(1-2p\),
so every recovery has error at least \(p\). The identity decoder attains
\(p\); hence \(\delta_{\rm rec}(E_p)=p\).

In the plane containing \(u\) and \(e_1\), the rank-one anchor has Bloch
coordinates \((s_d,0,-t_d)\), where
\(s_d=2\sqrt{d-1}/d\), \(t_d=(d-2)/d\), and \(s_d^2+t_d^2=1\).
The channel shrinks its transverse coordinate by \(c=1-2p\). Choose as
output effect the projection with Bloch vector
\(\beta(s_d/c,0,-t_d)\), where
\(\beta=(t_d^2+s_d^2/c^2)^{-1/2}\), and extend it by zero on the
orthogonal complement. Its pullback differs from the anchor by
\(e_d(p)=(1-\beta)/2\). Complement it for the positive \(Z_1\) test.
Thus \(\epsilon_{\mathcal R_d}(E_p)\le e_d(p)\).
Solving \(e=e_d(p)\), for \(e<1/2\), gives

\[
\mathfrak M_{\mathcal R_d}(e)\ge
f\left(\frac{(1-2e)^{-2}-1}{s_d^2}\right),
\qquad f(x)=\tfrac12(1-(1+x)^{-1/2}).
\]

The argument is at least \(de\); monotonicity and concavity give
\(f(de)\ge f(1)\min(1,de)\). For \(e\ge1/2\), use monotonicity of the
modulus. The upper bound is Theorem 5.1. ∎

**Proof of the geometric comparison.** At any amplification let
\(h=\max_R\|[X,R\otimes I]\|\). Because
\(Z_i=T_{1i}Z_1T_{1i}\), each off-diagonal block row of \(X\) has norm
at most \(3h/2\). Its row domain is the complement of that coordinate, so
orthogonal-range summation bounds the off-diagonal part by
\(\tfrac32\sqrt{d-1}h\). The \((i,j)\) block of \([X,T_{ij}]\) is
\(X_{ii}-X_{jj}\); the diagonal part is within \((d-1)h/d\) of its
normalized partial trace. Thus

\[
\Gamma_{\rm cb}\le\tfrac32\sqrt{d-1}+(d-1)/d.
\]

Testing (2.3) on \(|u\rangle\langle u|\) gives the lower bound
\(\sqrt{d-1}/2\). Algebraic span in radius four follows from
\(E_{ii}=(I-Z_i)/2\),
\(T_{ij}-I+E_{ii}+E_{jj}=E_{ij}+E_{ji}\), and
\(Z_iT_{ij}-I+E_{ii}+E_{jj}=E_{ji}-E_{ij}\).

Every length-\(\ell\) word is a signed permutation moving at most
\(2\ell\) coordinates. Let \(\Pi_{\rm off}=\sum_{i\ne j}|ij\rangle
\langle ij|\). Its expectation in \((R_w\otimes I)|\Omega\rangle\)
is at most \(2|w|/d\). Choi domination of \(T_\mu\) by
\(\lambda\mathrm{Dep}\) therefore forces
\(\mathbb E|w|\ge\lambda(d-1)/2\), and
\(M_2\ge\lambda^2(d-1)^2/4\). Since
\(\lambda/(1-\sqrt{1-\lambda})=1+\sqrt{1-\lambda}\), the coefficient
in (3.1) is at least \(3(d-1)^2/2\).
Conversely every signed permutation has length at most \(4d-3\), and
uniform averaging over them is exactly depolarizing. Constant-weight
minorization radius is therefore \(\Theta(d)\). ∎

The last statement limits this particular positive-averaging certificate,
not physical recovery itself. For the established comparison of cost-induced
mixing, cb mixing and CP return times, see [AJW, Section 3.3, Eq. (3.50)].
That hierarchy does not itself state our signed-family recovery separation.

## 6. Uniform recovery of an arbitrary logical qubit

### Theorem 6.1. Fixed-effect qubit recovery

For a finite qubit reflection family with scalar common commutant and fixed
effects \(Q_y\in M_m\), there is one decoder depending only on \(R,Q\) such
that every compatible channel satisfies

\[
\tfrac12\|D_{R,Q}E-\mathrm{id}_2\|_\diamond
\le\min\{1,1028\Gamma_{\rm cb}(R)^2e\}.
\tag{6.1}
\]

The decoder adds a factor-four clean space, extracts an exact Pauli algebra,
and discards its multiplicity. It requires spectral preprocessing, not a
promised efficient circuit.

The full proof is Appendix A, included in the complete review artifact.
Choose a pair of Bloch axes with maximal sine
\(s>0\), rotate logical coordinates so they are \(Z\) and \(cZ+sX\),
and dilate their effects to two physical reflections. A further doubling
allows a kernel-completed sign of their commutator that anticommutes exactly
with the first reflection. The same physical representation then works for
every compatible pullback. Two-sided CP defect estimates control the sign's
off-diagonal entry at order \(e/s^2\), rather than using a generic
square-root continuity estimate. The three Pauli bounds imply half-diamond
error below \(257e/s^2\), and \(\Gamma_{\rm cb}\ge1/(2s)\).

Extraction from supplied measurements is established in complementary-observable
recovery [R16,NMK25] and self-testing [SH16,SBWS18]. The commutator spectral
pairing used to identify a Pauli factor also appears in [K17, Proposition A.3].
Appendix A uses this representation mechanism and standard CP covariance
estimates [C74] to bound the recovered Pauli pullbacks linearly in operator
norm, hence in half-diamond distance. The quantitative conclusion includes
possibly oblique calibrated pairs; the extraction principle itself is prior.
The square-root obstruction in [SH16, Section III.3] additionally requires
post-measurement certification and does not obstruct the recovery channel here.

## 7. An executable decoder from seven coherent test types

### Lemma 7.1. Extracting an output while discarding leakage

Let \(J=J_D\otimes I_O\) be an isometry and \(P=JJ^*=P_D\otimes I_O\).
Compare an ideal unitary circuit \(W\) with a physical unitary circuit
\(\widetilde W\), containing \(L\) approximate steps and exact interspersed
gates that intertwine \(J\). Assume at step \(t\)

\[
\|J^*\widetilde G_tJ-G_t\|\le\delta_t,\quad
\|(I-P)\widetilde G_tJ\|\le\lambda_t^{\rm out},\quad
\|J^*\widetilde G_t(I-P)\|\le\lambda_t^{\rm in}.
\]

If the ideal circuit extracts the desired output into \(O\), the physical
one followed by discarding all of \(D\) has half-diamond distance from the
ideal retained-output channel at most

\[
\sum_t\delta_t+
\sum_t\lambda_t^{\rm in}\sum_{i<t}\lambda_i^{\rm out}
+\tfrac12\left(\sum_t\lambda_t^{\rm out}\right)^2.
\tag{7.1}
\]

**Proof.** For the prefix let
\(q_t=\|(I-P)\widetilde W_tJ\|\). Inserting \(P+(I-P)\) gives
\(q_t\le q_{t-1}+\lambda_t^{\rm out}\). Likewise, for
\(a_t=\|J^*\widetilde W_tJ-W_t\|\),
\(a_t\le a_{t-1}+\delta_t+\lambda_t^{\rm in}q_{t-1}\).
Thus \(a_L\) is bounded by the first two terms of (7.1).

After initializing \(O\), decompose the final isometry as \(JK+Z\), with
\(PZ=0\). Because \(P=P_D\otimes I_O\), all compressed/leakage cross
terms vanish on tracing \(D\), including with a reference: every retained
observable commutes with \(P\). The compressed CP contribution differs
from the ideal one in diamond norm by at most \(2a_L\); the leakage CP
contribution has diamond norm \(\|Z\|^2\le q_L^2\). Divide by two. ∎

There is no physical projection onto \(P\). Retaining any part of its
support instead of discarding it can invalidate the cross-term cancellation.

### Theorem 7.2. Cyclic coherent-tester extraction

Let \(n=3s\), and partition logical computational labels into
\((u,v,w)\in(\mathbb F_2^s)^3\). Let the seven test reflections be
\(X_1,Z_1,C_{12},C_{21},C_{23},C_{32},R\), where \(C_{ab}\) applies a
CNOT from coordinate \(a\) to \(b\) in every triple and \(R\) sends
\((u,v,w)\) to \((u,v+Su,w)\), with cyclic shift
\((Su)_i=u_{i+1\bmod s}\). These are among the explicit generators of
[ABHHT26, Theorem 2.2].

Suppose each output test is supplied by a reversible circuit \(B_y\) of at
most \(G\) elementary gates, padded to a common \(a\)-qubit workspace,
and acceptance is flag value one. There is one decoder \(D_{\mathbf B}\),
determined by the supplied tester circuits alone, such that every compatible
channel satisfies

\[
\tfrac12\|D_{\mathbf B}E-\mathrm{id}_{2^n}\|_\diamond
\le\min\{1,4(16n-14)^2e\}.
\tag{7.2}
\]

It uses \(32n-28\) forward/inverse tester calls, \(n+a\) initially clean
qubits, \(O(nG+n^2)\) ordinary gates and \(O(n^3+nG)\) classical
compilation work (apart from representation/addressing costs). It makes no
additional calls to \(E\), uses no postselection, and retains only the new
output register. No expander gap is required for this construction.

**Proof.** Put \(S_{ab}=C_{ab}C_{ba}C_{ab}\), so these swap coordinate
blocks. The seven-letter word \(U=RS_{12}S_{23}\), rightmost first,
acts by \((u,v,w)\mapsto(w,u+Sw,v)\), with binary matrix

\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&I\\I&0&S\\0&I&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]

For \(\overline S=\operatorname{diag}(S,S,S)\), direct multiplication gives
\(A^3+\overline SA+I=0\), hence \(\overline S=A^2+A^{-1}\).
Let \(f\) be the first coordinate of the \(u\) block. Its forward cyclic
space is invariant under \(A^{-1}\), since \(A\) is invertible on that
finite-dimensional invariant space. It therefore contains all shifts of
\(f,Af,A^2f\), which are the first coordinates of \(u,v,w\). Hence
\(f,Af,\ldots,A^{n-1}f\) form a basis. Transposing the recurrence proves
the same statement for \(A^T\): its first three powers on \(f\) occupy the
first coordinates of \(u,w,v\), and its cyclic space is invariant under
\(\overline S^T=(A^T)^2+(A^T)^{-1}\). The shifts fill all coordinates.
In either case, if the first \(n\) iterates were dependent, the first such
dependence would make the preceding span invariant and prevent it from
reaching dimension \(n\). Set

\[
F=A^{n-1},\quad
N=\begin{pmatrix}f^T\\f^TA\\\vdots\\f^TA^{n-1}\end{pmatrix},\quad
M=[A^{-(n-1)}f\ A^{-(n-2)}f\ \cdots\ f].
\tag{7.3}
\]

These are controllability and observability matrices over \(\mathbb F_2\).
Both \(M,N\) are invertible. The following record-then-erase transfer has
the same basic pattern as CSS-style coherent decoding [NMK25, Section III.1].
Append output \(O=|0^n\rangle\). Apply
Hadamards to \(O\), then for \(t=0,\ldots,n-1\) apply \(Z_1\)
controlled by \(O_t\), followed by \(U\) unless \(t=n-1\). Final
Hadamards give exactly \(|x\rangle|0\rangle\mapsto|Fx\rangle|Nx\rangle\),
because the phase on label \(b\) is \((-1)^{b^TNx}\).

Apply \(M^{-1}N^{-1}\) to \(O\), obtaining label \(c=M^{-1}x\).
Next apply \(X_1\) controlled by \(O_t\), followed by \(U^{-1}\)
unless \(t=n-1\). The final old logical label is
\(A^{-(n-1)}Fx+\sum_tc_tA^{-(n-1-t)}f=x+Mc=0\).
Apply \(M\) to \(O\). Thus the ideal circuit transfers every quantum
state coherently, with \(W(|\psi\rangle|0\rangle)=|0\rangle|\psi\rangle\).
It has \(L=2n+14(n-1)=16n-14\) reflection occurrences.

Replace each reflection by
\(\widehat R_y=B_y^*(2\Pi_y-I)B_y\). A controlled version uses the
unconditional \(B_y\), controlled middle phase, and unconditional
\(B_y^*\). For acceptance flag one that middle phase is
\(Z_{\rm control}\,\mathrm{CZ}_{\rm control,flag}\); omitting the first
sign would implement the wrong controlled reflection.

For analysis alone choose the padded Stinespring isometry \(V_0\) for
\(E\), including the tester workspace initially zero, and set
\(J=V_0\otimes I_O\). Each reflection's compressed discrepancy is
\(\delta_t\le2e\). Hermiticity and the identity

\[
(\widetilde GJ-JG)^*(\widetilde GJ-JG)
=2I-(J^*\widetilde GJ)G-G(J^*\widetilde GJ)
\]

give both leakage bounds at most \(2\sqrt e\). Controlled reflections
have the same blockwise estimates. Lemma 7.1 gives
\(2Le+4e(L^2-L/2)=4L^2e\).

The common tester workspace may be dirty between occurrences. Its arbitrary
off-subspace action is already covered by the lemma; no fresh promise or
reset is assumed. All noisy-output and workspace registers are finally
discarded, as is the inaccessible environment in the channel description.
The decoder never uses that environment or the analytical projector.

Each reflection uses two tester calls. Binary Gaussian elimination compiles
the two output linear maps with \(O(n^2)\) CNOT/SWAP gates and \(O(n^3)\)
classical work. Copying/reversing tester descriptions costs \(O(nG)\).
This proves the resources and uniformity. ∎

There are two distinct resource accounts. In the reversible black-box model,
count \(32n-28\) calls to testers or their inverses and \(O(n^2)\) additional
Clifford gates; a controlled tester call is not assumed. In the supplied
circuit-description model, expand those calls to obtain total gate count
\(O(nG+n^2)\) and copying/compilation work \(O(n^3+nG)\). The input channel's
output register is supplied, not counted among the \(n+a\) newly clean qubits.

If conversion to another gate alphabet requires approximation, synthesizing
each of \(N_g\) gates to operator error \(\eta/N_g\) adds at most \(\eta\)
to the half-diamond error by telescoping; use the actual gate model's
synthesis cost rather than identifying exact spectral preprocessing with an
efficient algorithm. With the supplied exact tester circuits and Clifford
additions, no new approximation is required.

The seven-type family is itself irreducible: its conjugated \(X_1,Z_1\)
directions span all binary Pauli coordinates by (7.3), and hence generate
the full matrix algebra. Theorem 4.1 supplies an \(\Omega(n^2e)\) minimax
obstruction for this fixed test count. Theorem 7.2 matches this error order
under coherent tester access. It does not bound the cost of obtaining those
testers from an unknown channel or from classical target advice.

## 8. Interpretation and limitations

**Generation is not a quantitative certificate.** The signed-permutation
family has algebraic span in radius four, yet its question error can be a
factor of order \(d\) smaller than its recovery error. Positive mixing and
direct extraction can have different costs even for that same family.

**Uniform recovery requires a fixed construction.** Optimizing a decoder after knowing
\(E\) does not justify swapping its quantifier with a family of channels.
The uniform anchor and qubit constructions avoid that issue by fixing their
operators from the effects before choosing \(E\) for analysis.

**Sharp effects are structural input.** They supply two small CP covariance
factors, so multiplying two calibrated sharp representatives can cost
\(O(e)\), not automatically \(O(\sqrt e)\). This local fact is not a
dimension-free bound on arbitrarily many products or on a global UCP section.

**Unused physical sectors must remain harmless.** Append an unused
two-dimensional sector to an exact four-dimensional encoding. Physical test
operators can have incompatible behavior on that sector while all pulled-back
logical tests and recovery remain exact. Thus a necessary recovery geometry
cannot demand small global physical commutators on irrelevant output space.

**The unresolved intrinsic question.** For general finite irreducible
reflection families, it remains open here whether
\(\delta_{\rm rec}(E)\le C\Gamma_{\rm cb}(R)^2\epsilon_R(E)\) with an
absolute constant. The uniform version, requiring one decoder from fixed
effects, is a distinct stronger target. The qubit and signed-permutation
results do not prove either claim in arbitrary dimension.

**Operational exclusions.** No result promises reusable or clean garbage,
an autonomous repeated-use apparatus, or a protocol deriving the calibration
premise from finitely many samples. The operator-norm premise is a mathematical
worst-input guarantee. The executable theorem assumes reversible coherent
tester access. It therefore supplies no unrestricted Aaronson–Kuperberg
unitary-synthesis result without a separate lawful tester construction.

# Appendix A. A decoder fixed by two oblique qubit effects

This appendix proves Theorem 6.1 of the main manuscript. All tensor identities
on Stinespring environments are suppressed when no confusion is possible.
No result in this appendix assumes access to that environment.

## A.1. Fix the decoder before choosing a channel

Discard scalar logical reflections. Write each remaining one as
\(R_y=n_y\cdot\sigma\). The finite irreducible family has a pair maximizing
\(s=|n_1\times n_2|>0\). A fixed logical unitary and orientation put this
pair in the form

\[
R_1=Z,\qquad R_2=cZ+sX,\qquad c^2+s^2=1.
\tag{A.1}
\]

For the two fixed physical effects put \(C_i=2Q_i-I\), and form the
Halmos reflection dilations on \(\mathbb C^{2m}\):

\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}C_1&\sqrt{I-C_1^2}\\
\sqrt{I-C_1^2}&-C_1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B=\begin{pmatrix}C_2&\sqrt{I-C_2^2}\\
\sqrt{I-C_2^2}&-C_2\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{A.2}
\]

Both square to identity. Double once more:
\(A'=A\oplus(-A)\), \(B'=B\oplus(-B)\), and
\(H'=(A'B'-B'A')/(2i)=H\oplus H\). Since
\(A'H'A'=-H'\), the first reflection exchanges the positive and negative
spectral spaces of \(H'\). On the nonzero spectrum choose the usual sign.
On the remaining space \(\ker H\oplus\ker H\), choose instead the
copy-exchange map \((\xi,\zeta)\mapsto(\zeta,\xi)\). The resulting
operator \(S\) obeys

\[
S=S^*,\quad S^2=I,\quad A'S=-SA',\quad H'=S|H'|.
\tag{A.3}
\]

The exchange rule is essential: arbitrary independent signs on zero modes
need not anticommute with \(A'\).

Two anticommuting reflections give an exact qubit representation. More
explicitly, \(S\) maps the positive eigenspace of \(A'\) isometrically
onto the negative one, so their dimensions agree. Choose bases related by
this map and adjust a phase. This produces a unitary
\(W:\mathbb C^{4m}\to\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^{2m}\) satisfying

\[
WA'W^*=Z\otimes I,\quad WSW^*=Y\otimes I,\quad
W(iA'S)W^*=X\otimes I.
\tag{A.4}
\]

Let \(J:\mathbb C^m\to\mathbb C^{4m}\) embed into the first copy, and
define

\[
D_{R,Q}(\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}_{2m}(WJ\rho J^*W^*).
\tag{A.5}
\]

Transform back by the fixed logical coordinate choice when necessary. This
is CPTP and depends only on the logical family and its fixed physical effects.
It has been defined before any noise channel, error parameter or Stinespring
representation is chosen.

## A.2. First and second moments under a compatible pullback

Now fix an arbitrary compatible \(E\). Let \(V\) be its Stinespring
isometry followed by \(J\), and write \(\phi(T)=V^*(T\otimes I)V\).
Then \(\phi\) is UCP and

\[
a=\phi(A'),\quad b=\phi(B'),\qquad
\|a-Z\|,\ \|b-(cZ+sX)\|\le2e.
\tag{A.6}
\]

For UCP maps the standard CP Schwarz/covariance estimate [C74] gives

\[
\|\phi(XY)-\phi(X)\phi(Y)\|
\le\|\phi(XX^*)-\phi(X)\phi(X)^*\|^{1/2}
\|\phi(Y^*Y)-\phi(Y)^*\phi(Y)\|^{1/2}.
\tag{A.7}
\]

Indeed insert \(I-VV^*\) between \(X,Y\) and use the two factor norms.
Since \(A',B'\) are reflections, their left and right defects coincide,
and \(\|I-a^2\|,\|I-b^2\|\le4e\).

Put \(U=A'B'\) and \(U_0=Z(cZ+sX)=cI+isY\). Equation (A.7) and
the two calibration errors yield \(\|\phi(U)-U_0\|\le8e\). Both
unitary defects of \(u=\phi(U)\) are at most \(16e\). Applying (A.7)
to \(U^2\), then comparing \(u^2\) with \(U_0^2\), gives

\[
\|\phi(U^2)-U_0^2\|\le32e,
\quad \|\phi(U^{*2})-U_0^{*2}\|\le32e.
\tag{A.8}
\]

As \(H'=(U-U^*)/(2i)\) and \(H'^2=(2I-U^2-U^{*2})/4\),

\[
\|h-sY\|\le8e,\qquad
\|k-s^2I\|\le16e,
\quad h=\phi(H'),\ k=\phi(H'^2).
\tag{A.9}
\]

Consequently

\[
\|H'V-sVY\|^2
=\|k-shY-sYh+s^2I\|\le32e=:q.
\tag{A.10}
\]

The completed sign \(S\) commutes with \(|H'|\) and preserves its kernel.
These estimates do not assume invertibility or a gap in the physical
commutator spectrum. The logical separation \(s>0\) is the only gap used.

## A.3. Sign rounding at linear error

Let \(\Pi_\pm=(I\pm S)/2\), \(G=|H'|\), and let
\(v_\pm=V|y_\pm\rangle\), where \(Y|y_\pm\rangle=\pm|y_\pm\rangle\).
On the wrong sign sector,
\((H'-s)\Pi_-v_+=-(G+s)\Pi_-v_+\). Thus (A.10) gives

\[
\|\Pi_-v_+\|^2,\quad\|\Pi_+v_-\|^2\le q/s^2.
\tag{A.11}
\]

This also handles the kernel, where the separation from the logical target
eigenvalue is exactly \(s\). The two diagonal entries of \(\phi(S)-Y\)
have modulus at most \(2q/s^2=64e/s^2\).

For its off-diagonal entry \(t=\langle v_+,Sv_-\rangle\), use

\[
\begin{aligned}
\langle v_+,H'v_-\rangle-st
={}&\langle\Pi_+v_+,(G-s)\Pi_+v_-\rangle\\
&-\langle\Pi_-v_+,(G-s)\Pi_-v_-\rangle.
\end{aligned}
\tag{A.12}
\]

In the first term, move the self-adjoint \(G-s\) onto \(\Pi_+v_+\),
whose residual norm is at most \(\sqrt q\); its other factor has norm
at most \(\sqrt q/s\). In the second term the residual acts on
\(\Pi_-v_-\), again a proper-sign factor of norm at most \(\sqrt q\),
and the remaining wrong-sign factor costs \(\sqrt q/s\). Thus the
right side of (A.12) has modulus at most \(2q/s\). Equation (A.9) also
gives \(|\langle v_+,H'v_-\rangle|\le8e\). Therefore

\[
|t|\le8e/s+2q/s^2\le72e/s^2.
\tag{A.13}
\]

Row-sum bounding the resulting Hermitian two-by-two matrix yields
\(\|\phi(S)-Y\|\le136e/s^2\).
For \(g=\phi(S)\), \(\|I-g^2\|\le272e/s^2\). Applying (A.7) to
\(A'S\) bounds its covariance by
\(\sqrt{4e\cdot272e/s^2}<33e/s\). Since \(iZY=X\),

\[
\|\phi(iA'S)-X\|\le2e+136e/s^2+33e/s\le171e/s^2.
\tag{A.14}
\]

All three recovered Pauli errors are thus at most \(171e/s^2\).

## A.4. Complete norm and geometry

For every amplification, write
\(T=I\otimes T_0+X\otimes T_x+Y\otimes T_y+Z\otimes T_z\).
Each coefficient is obtained by applying the norm-one functional
\(A\mapsto\tau_2(\sigma_jA)\) on the first factor; its completely
bounded norm is one. Hence \(\|T_j\|\le\|T\|\). The adjoint of
\(D_{R,Q}E-\mathrm{id}\) vanishes on \(I\), so

\[
\|D_{R,Q}E-\mathrm{id}\|_\diamond
=\|(D_{R,Q}E-\mathrm{id})^*\|_{\rm cb}
\le3\cdot171e/s^2.
\tag{A.15}
\]

The half-diamond bound is below \(257e/s^2\). If \(R_i\) is one member
of the selected maximizing pair, then
\(\|R_i-\tau_2(R_i)I\|=1\) and
\(\max_y\|[R_i,R_y]\|\le2s\). Therefore
\(\Gamma_{\rm cb}(R)\ge1/(2s)\), giving (6.1).

For each compatible \(E\), the proof chooses a possibly different
Stinespring witness but never changes (A.5). Thus the same decoder works
uniformly without a convexity assumption on the compatible family. The cap
by one treats all larger-error cases. Finiteness of the logical question
family ensures the maximizing pair exists.

## A.5. Resources and scope

The construction embeds the physical output of dimension \(m\) into
dimension \(4m\), equivalent to adding two clean qubits, applies a fixed
unitary identification and discards the multiplicity of dimension \(2m\).
There is no postselection, environmental access, extra channel use, or
channel-dependent correction. Exact square roots, a spectral sign, a kernel
split and the unitary identification are mathematical preprocessing. No
polynomial-time synthesis claim follows from their existence.
